newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kia shares plunge on affiliate's late debt payment.
newsitem.headline: Kia shares plunge on affiliate's late debt payment.

text.p: Shares of South Korea's Kia Group firms plunged on Tuesday as delayed debt payments by a commercial vehicle affiliate sparked concern the nation's eighth largest group faced financial problems.
All six listed Kia Group shares fell sharply after Asia Motors was late paying back 130 billion won ($146 million) in promissory notes due on Monday.
A group spokesman strongly denied Kia had financial problems.
But an Asia spokesman said it had encountered difficulties on Monday because its debt demands were higher than usual.
"We ran into trouble only temporarily. We settled all the problems," said the Asia spokesman.
Several merchant banking corporations rolled over notes worth 84 billion won for three months for Asia Motor.
Kia Motors, the flagship firm of the group, helped Asia to redeem about 30 billion won in debt obligation, officials at financial institutions said.
"We had temporary cash flow problems as other companies are experiencing. But we now have no financial trouble," said another Asia spokesman, Ahn Suk-woo.
Kia Motors' share price briefly hit its daily lower limit of 14,700 won, but late buying brought the price back to 15,300 won the close, down 600 won on the day.
The other five listed Kia affiliates, including Asia Motors, went limit down.
Analysts said Asia's profitablity had worsened over the past two years due to intensifying competition in the commercial vehicle market.
"Basically the domestic market is too small for so many companies," said Ji Sung-chul, analyst at LG Economic Research Institute.
South Korea's major business conglomerates, including the Hyundai Group, the Daewoo Group and the Samsung Group, are producing commercial vehicles.
Asia incurred losses of 27.4 billion won in 1996 on sales of 1.68 trillion won, compared to losses of 8.3 billion won in 1995 on sales of 1.61 trillion won.
Its debts totalled 2.24 trillion won at the end of 1996, against total assets of 2.68 trillion won.
Analysts said Kia Motors' financial status was well in line with the average of the nation's major conglomerates.
Kia Motors' total debts were estimated at 5.6 trillion won at the end of 1996, against its net worth of 1.3 trillion and its entire assets of 6.9 trillion won.

Separately, tensions between Kia Motors and upstart carmaker Samsung Motors Inc escalated on Tuesday, when Samsung refused to apologise in a dispute over the need to restructure the auto industry until prosecutors complete their probe.
"We are concerned about the real motives behind the pressure for an apology," said a Samsung spokesman.

Earlier on Tuesday, Hyundai Motor Co and five other South Korean automakers repeated their demand that Samsung publicly apologise for asserting in a report that there was a "managerial conflict" at Kia. Samsung also asserted Kia had reached its maximum growth potential.
"We don't want unnecessary discussion until the prosecution office comes up with the results of its investigation," the Samsung spokesman said.
"If we turn out to be innocent, the party that has caused the current problems should take all the responsibility," he said. He declined to elaborate.
Samsung said the report was an opinion by an individual employee and did not represent the company's official position, but Kia filed a complaint with prosecutors. ($1=888.50 won)
